raw_lines: • Most reliability comes from the harness
• The harness, not the model, is the control system
• Optimize for trust, not raw speed
Module 1 Code: Pre-Hook Interception & Loop Detection
• pre_execution_hook(command): regex inspection blocks destructive commands (rm -rf, sudo) before subprocess spawn.
• loop_detector(command): sliding-window history halts repeated identical failing commands when retries >= max_retries.
• Execution Safety: guarantees dangerous proposals never touch the filesystem or consume unlimited tokens.
• Pre-Action Interception: regex matching against dangerous patterns stops rm -rf before execution.
• Loop Breaking: tracking recent commands breaks retry traps and prevents infinite token burn.
• Un-harnessed run: deletes var/log/app.log and loops on failing pytest 3 times without recovery.
• Harnessed run: pytest runs once, 2nd attempt halted with LOOP_HALTED, rm -rf blocked with BLOCKED, sandbox logs preserved (log_survived=True).
• Five pillars of a production harness
• Policy is code, not a prompt
Module 2 Code: Tool Permissions & Post-Edit Audit
• validate_tool_permission(): enforces tool allowlist and blocks path traversal using is_relative_to().
• run_post_edit_hook(): inspects code proposals for API secrets (sk-proj-) and empty edits before writing.
• log_event(): records every check and decision to events.jsonl with ISO timestamps.
Module 2 Mechanics: Path Isolation & JSONL Audit
• Scoped Privilege: only allow registered tool set; deny unlisted tool requests before invocation.
• Path Sandboxing: Path.resolve().is_relative_to() prevents ../ escapes and sibling directory bypasses.
• ContextTokenBudgeter.compact_output() keeps 5 head and 15 tail lines, preventing compiler logs from swamping context.
• All operations are logged to events.jsonl as structured audit records.
• Feed pytest failures back to the agent
• Log every tool event to JSONL
• Vague: make it fast and safe
Module 3 Code: Scope & Non-Goal Spec Verifier
• Scope Verification: blocks edits to files outside the spec (e.g. database.py rejected).
• Non-Goal Enforcement: rejects diffs containing non-goal keywords (database, oauth2).
• AST Verification: ast.parse() ensures syntactically valid Python before acceptance.
Module 3 Mechanics: Scope Enforcement & AST Check
• Strict Scope Enforcement: attempt_write() verifies normalized paths against parsed SPEC.md allowed list.
• Non-Goal Filtering: prevents unrequested architectural shifts (e.g. adding database layers to a stateless JWT validator).
• ast.parse() validates syntax on all generated files before test execution, preventing broken builds.
• Acceptance criteria are verified against live pytest runs over the generated modules.
• Four control layers, not one prompt
• PreToolUse can allow, deny, ask, defer
• matcher is a tool name, e.g. Bash
• Scan for sk-proj- and AKIA keys
• acceptEdits: files yes, risky Bash no
• Replay fixed tasks from a known repo
• Keep the evaluator off the agent
Module 4 Code: PreToolUse Interceptor & AST Audit
• permission_output(): emits structured JSON for Claude Code's PreToolUse protocol.
• audit_ast_and_secrets(): parses AST syntax and scans for hardcoded API keys (sk-proj-, AKIA).
Module 4 Mechanics: Hook Protocol & Secret Scanning
• Programmatic Enforcement: hooks run as external processes; LLM prompts cannot bypass an exit-code 2 hook or deny response.
• PreToolUse Interception: dangerous flags (--dangerously-skip-permissions) are intercepted and rejected at the gateway.
• audit_ast_and_secrets() performs AST compilation before saving to disk to prevent syntax errors.
• Scans code proposals for secret patterns (OpenAI sk-proj-, AWS AKIA), preventing token leaks before commits.
• Risk tiers: auto, log, or confirm
• evaluate_request(): classifies requests by risk level (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL).
• Low-risk reads are auto-approved; medium-risk writes are audited.
• Critical tools (git_push) strictly require an approval entry in approvals.json.
Module 5 Mechanics: Approval Ledger & Audit Trail
• Human-in-the-Loop Safeguards: autonomous agents cannot unilaterally execute destructive or remote actions.
• Out-of-Band Approvals: critical requests look up a pre-approved request_id in approvals.json.
• Critical operations produce signed pending artifacts (pending_push.json) rather than invoking remote network calls directly.
• All permission evaluations and executions are recorded to audit.jsonl with UTC timestamps.
• How do you gate agent permissions?
• Which failure mode hurts you most?
• Where would a spec save a week?
• Keep every bug as a regression test
• Put the real failure in the prompt
Module 6 Code: TDA Pipeline & Traceback Feedback
• run_test_suite(): executes real pytest subprocess and captures stdout/stderr.
• format_fix_prompt(): formats raw pytest tracebacks directly into agent repair prompts.
• register_anti_regression_test(): permanently appends bug test cases to prevent regressions.
• Deterministic Ground Truth: subprocess execution ensures pytest runs against the real Python environment.
• Automated Feedback Loop: captures exact traceback (e.g. ZeroDivisionError) without human copy-paste.
• register_anti_regression_test() permanently appends every discovered edge-case to the test suite.
• Prevents 'fix-and-break' regressions where newer agent edits silently break existing features.
• MCP: tools and resources over stdio
• Can bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP
• Load in place or via marketplace
Module 7 Code: MCP Server & Client Runner
• MCPServer: exposes @mcp.tool() callable actions and @mcp.resource() read-only data URIs.
• StdioServerParameters: launches server subprocess communicating via JSON-RPC stdio streams.
• ClientSession: handles initialize handshake, tool discovery, tool calls, and resource reads.
Module 7 Mechanics: Stdio Protocol & Capability Discovery
• Tools vs. Resources: tools represent callable actions with side effects; resources represent read-only URI data.
• SDK 2.x Authoring: uses MCPServer rather than legacy FastMCP wrappers.
• ClientSession initializes session -> calls tools/list to inspect schemas -> executes tools/call with typed arguments.
• Resources are read-only documents queried via standard URIs (config://app-settings).
• Each subagent has a clean window
• Agent tool; Task is an alias
Module 8 Code: Git Worktree Isolation & Sub-Spec Extractor
• WorktreeIsolation: creates dedicated git worktrees and branches for isolated implementer workspaces.
• SubagentPromptIsolator: filters master spec to pass only task-relevant lines, preventing context bloat.
• MultiAgentTeam: coordinates Planner (design), Implementer (isolated write), and Reviewer (AST/tests).
Module 8 Mechanics: Isolated Worktrees & Telemetry Loop
• True Git Sandboxing: WorktreeIsolation isolates edits to dedicated branches, preventing main branch pollution.
• Focused Subagent Contexts: passing only sub-spec slices keeps subagent context windows lean and focused.
• The Reviewer audits code in a clean context window, eliminating confirmation bias.
• Telemetry logging (telemetry.jsonl) records error patterns to guide ongoing AGENTS.md refinements.
• Agree the spec before any code
• Failures go back into the loop

class FiveStepSOPPipeline:
    def run_pipeline(self, feature_name: str) -> int:
        # Step 1: Spec First
        allowed_files, non_goals = parse_spec(self.spec_path)

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="module09_pipeline_") as temp:
            workspace = Path(temp)
            # Step 2: Constrained Execution
            enforcer = ScopeEnforcer(workspace, allowed_files)
            enforcer.attempt_write("auth_validator.py", implementation)
            enforcer.attempt_write("database.py", "...")  # BLOCKED: Out-of-scope

            # Step 3: Deterministic Checks
            engine = GuardrailsEngine(workspace)
            engine.audit_ast_and_secrets("auth_validator.py", implementation)
            engine.intercept_shell_command("sudo rm -rf /var/config")  # BLOCKED

            # Step 4: Test Verification
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "tests/test_auth.py", "-q"], cwd=workspace)

            # Step 5: Human Review & Diff
            diff = difflib.unified_diff(original.splitlines(), implementation.splitlines())
raw_lines: • Orchestrates all 5 steps into a single verifiable execution pipeline.
• Rejects out-of-scope files, blocks dangerous shell commands, and verifies AST syntax.
• Runs real pytest subprocesses and renders clean unified diffs for human review.
Module 9 Mechanics: Pipeline Orchestration & PR Review
• Sequential Gate Verification: no code lands without passing every gate (Spec -> Scope -> Hooks -> Tests -> Review).
• Objective Pass/Fail Evidence: all checks are backed by real subprocess exits and AST inspections.
Human Review as the Final Barrier
• Step 5 generates unified diffs (difflib.unified_diff) for human review before any merge.
• PR merges remain strictly out-of-band to preserve engineer accountability.
• ProductionHarnessAuditor: evaluates 5 objective readiness gates across the codebase.
• Audits memory files, PreToolUse settings, test runner validity, MCP tool declarations, and subagents.
• Replaces subjective assertions with evidence-backed inspection.
Module 10 Mechanics: Readiness Scorecard & Audit Gates
• Objective Repository Auditing: inspects configuration files, AST node trees, and scripts programmatically.
• Five Audit Gates: Memory files (1), PreToolUse hooks (2), Automated test runner (3), MCP tool/resource declarations (4), and Subagent definitions (5).
• Masterclass repository achieves 100% PASS across all five readiness gates.
• Readily integrable into CI/CD pipelines to prevent harness regressions before agent deployment.
